[BBC Business] Nvidia dismisses 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex CEO
A number of tech figures have backed an effort asking the AI chip giant to give Jensen Huang his job back.

[BBC Business] Create more jobs for under-25s by cutting National Insurance, key report urges
Some parents are so desperate for their children to find a job that they've offered to pay their wages, one hairdresser has told the BBC.

[BBC Business] Faisal Islam: What's in the Brexit reset food deal and are there trade-offs?
EU minister Hamish Falconer insists Britain would have some influence on policy as part of a new deal.

[BBC Business] Intel sued by investors after PC sales slump hits share price
A proposed class action claims the firm hid the impact of slowing PC sales from shareholders.

[CNBC] Trump’s accounts traded up to $97.5 million in Nvidia as Huang gained White House access
Trump’s accounts sold up to $1 million in Nvidia stock five days after he was briefed on Jensen Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.

[CNBC] JPMorgan Chase says temporary software bug is affecting consumer banking
CNBC's Eamon Javers reported there was no indication of bad actors involved and likewise no indication that a bug was impacting multiple banks at the same time.

[CNBC] Berkshire Hathaway raised its stake in Delta in the third quarter. It also trimmed a key bank holding
Berkshire Hathaway added to several stock positions in the third quarter while trimming others, including Bank of America.

[CNBC] United Airlines reports system outage affecting departing flights
United Airlines said Monday that a widespread system outage was affecting departing flights.

[MarketWatch] Berkshire upped its bet on a beleaguered U.S. housing market, while souring on these bank stocks
Berkshire Hathaway stepped up its investments in the U.S. housing market last quarter, nearly doubling its stake in home builder Lennar.

[MarketWatch] ‘He calls my plans a fantasy’: My husband says we can’t afford a $200,000-a-year retirement. Is he being cheap?
“We have $2 million saved in our retirement accounts and a house worth $1.3 million.”

[MarketWatch] The FDA declined to approve one of biotech’s most closely watched cancer drugs. The company’s stock tumbled.
The regulator told Summit Therapeutics that the lung-cancer drug needs to prove it can help people live longer.

[MarketWatch] ‘It leaves me with a sour taste’: My elderly mother gave our cousin $800 for a car repair. Should I be worried?
“I know older people can easily feel patronized, and I don’t want that to happen.”
